user.title: Sign in to eufy (once)
user.description: eufy's cloud is used only now, to fetch the lock's keys; after that the lock is controlled over your network. Use a separate eufy account that the lock is shared with: signing in elsewhere with the same account ends this session.

host.title: Where is {name}?
host.description: The lock's IP address on your network. Give it a fixed address (a DHCP reservation in your router) so it is always found. Leave empty to search the network.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to eufy again
reauth_confirm.description: eufy needs the password for {email} again.

error.invalid_auth: eufy rejected the email or password.
error.invalid_code: eufy rejected that code. Sign in again for a new one.

data.cloud_wake: Wake the lock through eufy's servers

data_description.poll_minutes: A check over your network only: it never wakes the lock through eufy, so it finds the lock only while it is awake (for example just after the keypad is used).
data_description.cloud_wake: On (default): eufy's servers nudge a sleeping lock awake only when you lock or unlock it from Home Assistant, and once at start-up; the commands themselves still go only over your network. Off: no eufy contact at all after setup, but a sleeping lock will not answer.
data_description.keep_connected: Holds the network session open with a silent status check every 10 s, so the lock stays awake: instant updates from the door and no further wakes through eufy unless the link drops. Uses more battery.
